directAnswer: You can find your subnet mask in the network settings of your device or by using command line tools like 'ipconfig' on Windows or 'ifconfig' on macOS/Linux.
summary: Finding your subnet mask is essential for understanding your network configuration and connectivity.

sections.heading: Understanding Subnet Mask
sections.body: A subnet mask is used to divide an IP address into network and host portions. It typically appears in the format of four octets (e.g., 255.255.255.0).

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: The method to find your subnet mask can vary depending on your operating system.

steps.title: Windows
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. Look for 'Subnet Mask' under your active network connection.

steps.title: macOS
steps.detail: Open System Preferences, go to 'Network', select your active connection, and find the subnet mask in the details.

steps.title: Linux
steps.detail: Open a terminal and type 'ifconfig' or 'ip addr'. Look for 'netmask' in the output for your active network interface.

faqs.question: What does a subnet mask do?
faqs.answer: A subnet mask defines the range of IP addresses that can be used within a network and helps route traffic appropriately.

faqs.question: Can I change my subnet mask?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can change your subnet mask in your network settings, but ensure it aligns with your network configuration to avoid connectivity issues.

faqs.question: Is the subnet mask the same as the IP address?
faqs.answer: No, the subnet mask is different from the IP address; it is used to determine which part of the IP address is the network and which part is the host.

caveats: The method to find the subnet mask may vary based on the version of the operating system.
